subject: chem
title: Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
syllabus: Tetravalency of carbon; shapes of simple molecules — hybridisation (s and p); classification of organic compounds based on functional groups and those containing halogens, oxygen, nitrogen and sulphur; homologous series; isomerism — structural and stereoisomerism. Nomenclature (trivial and IUPAC). Covalent bond fission — homolytic and heterolytic: free radicals, carbocations and carbanions; stability of carbocations and free radicals, electrophiles and nucleophiles. Electronic displacement in a covalent bond — inductive effect, electromeric effect, resonance and hyperconjugation. Common types of organic reactions — substitution, addition, elimination and rearrangement.

body: Principal group (suffix): acid > anhydride > ester > acid halide > amide > nitrile > aldehyde > ketone > alcohol > amine > alkene/alkyne
Parent = longest chain holding the principal group (and most multiple bonds). Number for the lowest locant to the suffix, then C=C/C≡C, then prefixes.
Prefixes (halo, nitro, alkyl, alkoxy) are listed alphabetically, ignoring di/tri. On a tie in locants, the group first in the alphabet gets the lower number.
Classes: acyclic (open chain), alicyclic (non-aromatic rings), aromatic (benzenoid and heterocyclic like pyridine, furan, pyrrole).

check.why: -ol is principal; on a tie the ene gets the lower number.

body: Chain (skeleton differs), position (group/bond position), functional (different groups: aldehyde/ketone, alcohol/ether, acid/ester, cyanide/isocyanide), metamers (different alkyl groups on either side of –O–, –CO–, –NH–), tautomers (keto ⇌ enol, needs α-H).
Alkane isomers: C_{4} 2, C_{5} 3, C_{6} 5, C_{7} 9, C_{8} 18. Monochlorides = number of different kinds of H.
Stereoisomers ≤ 2^{n}, n = chiral centres + stereo C=C. Two identical chiral centres (2,3-dichlorobutane) → 3 (RR, SS, meso)
Chiral carbon: four different groups. Cis/trans needs two different groups on EACH alkene carbon (propene and 2-methylbut-2-ene have none).
cis-But-2-ene has a dipole moment; trans is more stable and has a higher melting point.
Inductive (σ, permanent, fades with distance): −I NO_{2} > CN > F > Cl > Br > I > OH; +I alkyl groups.
Resonance/mesomeric (π, permanent): +R –OH, –OR, –NH_{2}, –X; −R –NO_{2}, –CN, –CHO, –COOH. Electromeric: temporary, only when a reagent attacks (+E: electrons move towards the reagent).
Hyperconjugation: σ(C–H) ↔ adjacent p/π; number of α-H. Explains 3° > 2° > 1° cations and alkene stability (more substituted = more stable, lower heat of hydrogenation).
Carbocation: sp^{2}, planar, 6 e^{−}, electrophile. Order: tropylium/trityl > benzyl ≈ allyl > 3° > 2° > 1° > CH_{3}^{+} > vinyl.
Carbanion: sp^{3}, pyramidal, 8 e^{−}, nucleophile; stabilised by −I/−R groups and by more s-character (sp > sp^{2} > sp^{3}).
Radical: 7 e^{−}, from homolysis; stability like carbocations. Aromatic: planar, cyclic, conjugated, 4n + 2 π e^{−}; 4n → antiaromatic.
Homolysis → radicals; heterolysis → ions. Nucleophiles donate a pair (OH^{−}, NH_{3}, CN^{−}, H_{2}O, π bonds); electrophiles accept (H^{+}, NO_{2}^{+}, BF_{3}, AlCl_{3}, C=O carbon).
Types: substitution (S_{N}, S_{E}, free radical), addition (electrophilic to C=C, nucleophilic to C=O), elimination, rearrangement.
Nucleophilicity: same atom → follows basicity; in protic solvents larger, less solvated ions win (I^{−} > Br^{−} > Cl^{−} > F^{−}).

traps: Trans-alkenes: higher m.p., lower dipole moment.
More substituted alkenes have LOWER heat of hydrogenation.

pyq.q: Number of optical isomers possible for 2 – chlorobutane
sol: C-2 carries H, Cl, CH_{3} and C_{2}H_{5} — one chiral centre.
2^{1} = 2 optical isomers (a pair of enantiomers).

pyq.q: Total number of isomeric compounds (including stereoisomers) formed by monochlorination of 2 - methylbutane is
sol: 2-Methylbutane has 4 kinds of H → 4 structural monochlorides.
1-chloro-2-methylbutane (chiral, 2) + 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (1) + 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (chiral, 2) + 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (1) = 6.

pyq.q: Identify the correct statements from the following. (A) Pentan-2-one and pentan-3-one are metamers (B) Butanenitrile (CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}CN) and butyl isocyanide (CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}NC) are functional isomers (C) Pentan-1-ol and 2-methylbutan-1-ol are position isomers (D) Butan-1-amine and diethylamine (CH_{3}CH_{2}NHCH_{2}CH_{3}) are homologous
sol: A: same C=O group, different alkyl groups on either side → metamers ✓. B: –CN vs –NC are different functional groups ✓.
C: the carbon chain differs (straight vs branched) → chain isomers, not position ✗.
D: same formula C_{4}H_{11}N → isomers (functional/metamers), not homologues ✗.

pyq.q: The total number of structural isomers possible for the substituted benzene derivatives with the molecular formula C_{9}H_{12} is ______ .
sol: Three extra carbons on a benzene ring: n-propyl, isopropyl (1 each); ethyl + methyl (o, m, p: 3); three methyls (1,2,3-; 1,2,4-; 1,3,5-: 3).
Total 8.

pyq.q: The number of different chain isomers for C_{7}H_{16} is ______.
sol: Heptane isomers: heptane; 2- and 3-methylhexane; 2,2-, 2,3-, 2,4-, 3,3-dimethylpentane; 3-ethylpentane; 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.
All 9 differ only in the carbon skeleton → 9 chain isomers.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Pair of Compounds) with List - II (Isomerism): (A) n-propanol and Isopropanol (B) Methoxypropane and ethoxyethane (C) Propanone and propanal (D) Neopentane and Isopentane; (I) Metamerism (II) Chain Isomerism (III) Position Isomerism (IV) Functional Isomerism
sol: Propan-1-ol/propan-2-ol: OH position. CH_{3}OC_{3}H_{7}/C_{2}H_{5}OC_{2}H_{5}: metamers.
Ketone/aldehyde: functional isomers. Neopentane/isopentane: chain isomers.

pyq.q: The incorrect statement regarding the geometrical isomers of 2-butene is :
sol: In trans-2-butene the two C–CH_{3} dipoles cancel (μ ≈ 0); cis has a net dipole. So "cis has less dipole moment" is wrong.
Rotation about C=C needs bond breaking, trans is less crowded (more stable), and they are stereoisomers.
o: cis-2-butene and trans-2-butene are not interconvertible at room temperature.
cis-2-butene has less dipole moment than trans-2-butene.
trans-2-butene is more stable than cis-2-butene.

pyq.q: Consider the isomers of hydrocarbon with molecular formula C_{5}H_{10}. These isomers do not decolourise KMnO_{4} solution. These isomers are subjected to chlorination with chlorine in presence of light to give monochloro compounds. The total number of monochloro compounds (structural isomers only) formed is _______ .
sol: No reaction with KMnO_{4} → saturated rings: cyclopentane, methylcyclobutane, 1,1- and 1,2-dimethylcyclopropane, ethylcyclopropane.
Kinds of H: 1 + 4 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 14 monochlorides.

pyq.q: Identify correct statements from the following : A. Propanal and propanone are functional isomers. B. Ethoxyethane and methoxypropane are metamers. C. But-2-ene shows optical isomerism. D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene are functional isomers. E. Pentane and 2,2-dimethyl propane are chain isomers.
sol: C ✗: but-2-ene has no chiral carbon (it shows geometrical isomerism). D ✗: same functional group, different C=C position → position isomers.
A, B, E are correct.

pyq.q: Match List - I (Pair of Compounds) with List - II (Type of Isomers): A. 2-Methylpropene and but-1-ene B. Cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene C. 2-Butanol and diethyl ether D. But-1-ene and but-2-ene; I. Stereoisomers II. Position isomers III. Chain isomers IV. Functional group isomers
sol: Branched vs straight chain → chain; cis/trans → stereoisomers; alcohol vs ether → functional; C=C position → position.

pyq.q: The incorrect statements regarding geometrical isomerism are : (A) Propene shows geometrical isomerism. (B) Trans isomer has identical atoms/groups on the opposite sides of the double bond. (C) Cis-but-2-ene has higher dipole moment than trans-but-2-ene. (D) 2-methylbut-2-ene shows two geometrical isomers. (E) Trans-isomer has lower melting point than cis isomer.
sol: A ✗: CH_{2}= end has two H. D ✗: one end carries two CH_{3}. E ✗: trans packs better → higher m.p.
B and C are correct statements. Incorrect: A, D, E.

pyq.q: How many different stereoisomers are possible for the given molecule? CH_{3}–CH(OH)–CH=CH–CH_{3}
sol: One chiral carbon (C-2) and one C=C with two different groups at each end (E/Z).

pyq.q: Propane molecule on chlorination under photochemical condition gives two di-chloro products, "x" and "y". Amongst "x" and "y", "x" is an optically active molecule. How many tri-chloro products (consider only structural isomers) will be obtained from "x" when it is further treated with chlorine under the photochemical condition?
sol: x = 1,2-dichloropropane (chiral C-2).
Its three different C–H positions (C-1, C-2, C-3) give 1,1,2-, 1,2,2- and 1,2,3-trichloropropane → 3.

pyq.q: RBr → (i) Mg, dry ether (ii) H_{2}O → 2-Methylbutane. The maximum number of RBr producing 2-methylbutane by above sequence of reactions is ______ (Consider the structural isomers only)
sol: RMgBr + H_{2}O → RH: Br can sit on any carbon of 2-methylbutane that bears H.
2-Methylbutane has 4 different kinds of carbon-H → 4 bromides.

pyq.q: The possible number of stereoisomers for 5-phenylpent-4-en-2-ol is ________.
sol: CH_{3}–CH(OH)–CH_{2}–CH=CH–Ph: one chiral carbon (C-2) and one E/Z double bond.

pyq.q: Total number of compounds with Chiral carbon atoms from following is: 2-methylcyclohexanone, cyclopentane-1,3-dione, CH_{3}–CH_{2}–CH(NO_{2})–COOH, CH_{3}–CH_{2}–CHBr–CH_{2}–CH_{3}, CH_{3}–CH(I)–CH_{2}–NO_{2}, CH_{3}–CH_{2}–CH(OH)–CH_{2}OH, CH_{3}–CH(CH_{3})–CH(I)–C_{2}H_{5}
sol: Chiral: 2-methylcyclohexanone (C-2), 2-nitrobutanoic acid, 2-iodo-1-nitropropane, butane-1,2-diol, 3-iodo-2-methylpentane.
Not chiral: cyclopentane-1,3-dione, 3-bromopentane (two ethyls). Total 5.

pyq.q: Which one of the following will show geometrical isomerism?
sol: Each end of the C=C needs two different groups.
=CH_{2} ends fail. With =CHBr, the ring carbon must have two different ring arms: a 4-Br ring is symmetric (both arms the same), a 3-Br ring is not → only the 3-bromo compound.

pyq.q: Isomeric hydrocarbons → negative Baeyer's test (Molecular formula C_{9}H_{12}). The total number of isomers from above with four different non-aliphatic substitution sites is –
sol: Negative Baeyer test → no C=C: the 8 alkylbenzenes C_{9}H_{12}.
Count kinds of ring C–H: o- and m-ethyltoluene have 4; propyl/isopropylbenzene 3, p-ethyltoluene 2, trimethylbenzenes 1–3. → 2.

pyq.q: 2-chlorobutane + Cl_{2} → C_{4}H_{8}Cl_{2} (isomers). Total number of optically active isomers shown by C_{4}H_{8}Cl_{2}, obtained in the above reaction is ______.
sol: Products: 1,2- (chiral: 2), 2,2- (achiral), 2,3- (two like centres: RR, SS active + meso) and 1,3-dichlorobutane (chiral: 2).
Optically active: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

pyq.q: Number of isomeric products formed by monochlorination of 2-methylbutane in presence of sunlight is ______.
sol: 4 structural monochlorides; two of them (1-chloro-2-methylbutane, 2-chloro-3-methylbutane) are chiral and come as 2 enantiomers each.

pyq.q: n-Butane on monochlorination under photochemical condition gives an optically active compound "P". "P" on further chlorination gives dichloro compounds. The number of dichloro compounds obtained (ignore stereoisomers) is :
sol: P = 2-chlorobutane. Its 4 different C–H positions give 1,2-, 2,2-, 2,3- and 1,3-dichlorobutane → 4.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: 2,6-diethylcyclohexanone and 6-methyl-2-n-propylcyclohexanone are metamers. Statement II: 2,2,6,6 - tetramethylcyclohexanone exhibits keto-enol tautomerism. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: same C_{11}H_{20}O ring ketone, different alkyl groups on the two sides of C=O → metamers. True.
II: both α-carbons carry two CH_{3} and no H → no enol can form. False.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Identify the correct IUPAC name of hydrocarbon (x) containing three primary carbon atoms and with molar mass 72 g mol^{−1}.
sol: M = 72 → C_{5}H_{12} (cyclopropanes C_{5}H_{10} are 70).
Primary carbons (bonded to one C): pentane 2, 2-methylbutane 3, neopentane 4 → 2-methylbutane.

pyq.q: Which of the following compound will most easily be attacked by an electrophile?
sol: Ring activation: –OH (strong +R) ≫ –CH_{3} (+I, hyperconjugation) > –H > –Cl (−I beats +R).
Phenol is attacked most easily.

pyq.q: The functional group that shows negative resonance effect is:
sol: –NH_{2}, –OH, –OR donate a lone pair into the ring (+R).
–COOH has a C=O that withdraws π electrons (−R).

pyq.q: Consider the compound (X): H–C(I)≡C(II)–CH_{2}(II)–CH(III)(CH_{3})–CH_{3}(IV), i.e. H–C≡C–CH_{2}–CH(CH_{3})–CH_{3} with C–H bonds labelled I (alkyne C–H), II (CH_{2}), III (CH) and IV (CH_{3}). The most stable and least stable carbon radicals, respectively, produced by homolytic cleavage of corresponding C - H bond are :
sol: II gives a propargylic radical, delocalised over the C≡C → most stable (more than tertiary III).
I gives an sp alkynyl radical (electron in an sp orbital, no delocalisation) → least stable.

pyq.q: Designate whether each of the following is aromatic or not: (a) cyclopentadienyl anion (b) cyclopentadienyl cation (c) cyclobutadiene dication (d) cyclobutadiene dianion (e) tropylium (cycloheptatrienyl) cation (f) cyclooctatetraene (g) cyclobutadiene (h) cyclopropenyl cation
sol: Hückel: planar, fully conjugated ring with 4n + 2 π electrons.
a (6), c (2), d (6), e (6), h (2) are aromatic; b (4) and g (4) are antiaromatic; f (8) is tub-shaped, non-aromatic.
o: b, e, f, g aromatic and a, c, d, h not aromatic
e, g aromatic and a, b, c, d, f, h not aromatic
a, b, c, d aromatic and e, f, g, h not aromatic
a, c, d, e, h aromatic and b, f, g not aromatic

pyq.q: The least acidic compound, among the following is: (A) 3-ethoxyphenol (B) benzenesulphonic acid (C) propanoic acid (D) ethyl propiolate, HC≡C–CO_{2}Et
sol: pKa: PhSO_{3}H ≈ −3 < propanoic acid 4.9 < phenol ≈ 10 < terminal alkyne C–H ≈ 25.
The ester's only acidic H is the ≡C–H → least acidic (D).

pyq.q: What will be the decreasing order of basic strength of the following conjugate bases? ^{−}OH, RO^{−}, CH_{3}COO^{−}, Cl^{−}
sol: Weaker acid ⇒ stronger conjugate base. pKa: ROH ≈ 16 > H_{2}O 15.7 > CH_{3}COOH 4.76 > HCl ≈ −7.

pyq.q: The correct sequence of acidic strength of the following aliphatic acids in their decreasing order is : CH_{3}CH_{2}COOH, CH_{3}COOH, CH_{3}CH_{2}CH_{2}COOH, HCOOH
sol: Alkyl groups push electrons (+I) and destabilise the carboxylate.
H (no +I) > CH_{3} > C_{2}H_{5} > C_{3}H_{7}: HCOOH is strongest.

pyq.q: The correct stability order of the following resonance structures of CH_{3}–CH=CH–CHO is: I: CH_{3}–C^{−}H–CH=C(–O^{+})–H [negative charge on carbon, positive on oxygen] II: CH_{3}–C^{+}H–CH=C(–O^{−})–H [positive charge on carbon, negative on oxygen] III: CH_{3}–CH=CH–CH=O [neutral]
sol: No charge separation (III) is best.
Of the charged ones, II puts the − charge on the more electronegative O; I puts + on O with only a sextet nearby → least stable. III > II > I.

pyq.q: Correct order of basic strength of Pyrrole, Pyridine and Piperidine is:
sol: Piperidine: sp^{3} N lone pair, free. Pyridine: sp^{2} lone pair (more s character, held tighter).
Pyrrole: the lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet → hardly basic.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement (I) : Benzyl chloride reacts faster in S_{N}1 mechanism than ethyl chloride. Statement (II) : Ethyl carbocation intermediate is less stabilized by hyperconjugation than benzyl carbocation by resonance. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: The benzyl cation is delocalised over the ring (resonance), far better than ethyl cation's 3 C–H hyperconjugation.
So benzyl chloride ionises faster. Both true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: For the molecule x = benzanilide, C_{6}H_{5}–CO–NH–C_{6}H_{5}, label the positions: on the ring attached to C=O, "p" = ortho and "r" = meta; on the ring attached to N, "s" = ortho and "u" = para. The preferred site for the attack of the electrophile is :
sol: The N-ring carries –NHCOPh: the N lone pair activates it (o/p director). The other ring carries –CONHPh, a deactivating meta director.
So attack is on the N-ring; para (u) beats ortho (s) because the group is bulky.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : In O_{2}N–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{+}H–C_{6}H_{4}–OCH_{3} (both para), the carbocation is stabilised by +R effect of –OCH_{3} group. Statement II : In O_{2}N–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{−}H–C_{6}H_{4}–OCH_{3}, the carbanion is stabilised by –R effect of –NO_{2} group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: p-OCH_{3} donates its lone pair through the ring onto the C^{+}.
p-NO_{2} pulls the C^{−} electron pair through the ring. Both true.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: The most stable carbocation from the following is :
sol: Para –OCH_{3} gives +R directly to the benzylic C^{+}; para –CH_{3} only hyperconjugation.
At meta, –OCH_{3} can only act by −I → destabilising.

pyq.q: The correct stability order of the following species/molecules is: p = cyclopropenyl anion, q = cyclopentadienyl anion, r = cyclooctatetraene
sol: q: 6π, planar → aromatic. r: 8π but tub-shaped → non-aromatic.
p: 4π planar cyclic → antiaromatic (least stable). q > r > p.

pyq.q: Which one of the carbocations from the following is most stable?
sol: All are allylic. In (2) the O lone pair is conjugated through C=C with the C^{+} (extended +R) — best.
In the ester the O lone pair is shared with its own C=O; F is strongly −I; in (1) the O is insulated by CH_{2} (−I only).

pyq.q: The correct order of stability of following carbocations is : A = Ph_{3}C^{+}, B = Ph_{2}CH^{+}, C = tropylium (cycloheptatrienyl) cation, D = CH_{3}CH_{2}C^{+}HCH_{3}
sol: Tropylium is aromatic (6π) — exceptionally stable.
Then delocalisation over three rings (Ph_{3}C^{+}) > two rings > a 2° alkyl cation.

pyq.q: The difference in energy between the actual structure and the lowest energy resonance structure for the given compound is
sol: The hybrid is lower in energy than any single contributor; that gap is the resonance (delocalisation) energy.

pyq.q: The interaction between π bond and lone pair of electrons present on an adjacent atom is responsible for
sol: Lone pair ↔ π conjugation (e.g. in vinyl ethers, aniline) is the resonance (mesomeric) effect.
Hyperconjugation is σ(C–H)–π overlap.

pyq.q: Given below are some nitrogen containing compounds: p-nitroaniline, benzylamine (C_{6}H_{5}CH_{2}NH_{2}), acetanilide (C_{6}H_{5}NHCOCH_{3}), aniline. Each of them is treated with HCl separately. 1.0 g of the most basic compound will consume ______ mg of HCl. (Given molar mass in g mol^{−1} C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, Cl : 35.5 )
sol: Benzylamine: the N lone pair is not delocalised into the ring (CH_{2} in between) → most basic. The others are aryl amines/amide.

pyq.q: Which among the following halides will generate the most stable carbocation in the nucleophilic substitution reaction?
sol: Ph_{3}C^{+} spreads the charge over three rings.
Benzyl (one ring) < trityl; 2° cyclohexyl and a primary homoallylic cation are far worse.

pyq.q: A species having carbon with sextet of electrons and can act as electrophile is called
sol: Carbocation: 3 bonds, 6 valence electrons, empty p orbital → electrophile. Radical has 7, carbanion 8.

pyq.q: IUPAC name of the some alkenes are given below. Find out the correct stability order. A. 2-Methylbut-2-ene B. cis-But-2-ene C. 2,3-Dimethylbut-2-ene D. Prop-1-ene
sol: More alkyl groups on the C=C → more hyperconjugation → more stable.
Tetra- (C) > tri- (A) > di- (B) > monosubstituted (D).

pyq.q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: (CH_{3})_{3}C^{+} is more stable than C^{+}H_{3} as nine hyperconjugation interactions are possible in (CH_{3})_{3}C^{+}. Statement II: C^{+}H_{3} is less stable than (CH_{3})_{3}C^{+} as only three hyperconjugation interactions are possible in C^{+}H_{3}. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
sol: I: 3 CH_{3} groups × 3 α-H = 9 hyperconjugative structures. True.
II: CH_{3}^{+} has no α-C–H at all → zero hyperconjugation (its own C–H bonds are in the nodal plane of the empty p). False.
o: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: Arrange the following carbanions in the decreasing order of stability. I. p-Br–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{−}H_{2} II. C_{6}H_{5}–C^{−}H_{2} III. p-CH_{3}O–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{−}H_{2} IV. p-CHO–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{−}H_{2} V. p-CH_{3}–C_{6}H_{4}–C^{−}H_{2}
sol: Electron-withdrawing para groups stabilise a carbanion; σ_{p}: CHO +0.42 (−R), Br +0.23 (−I), H 0, CH_{3} −0.17, OCH_{3} −0.27 (+R).
IV > I > II > V > III.

pyq.q: Find out the statements which are not true. A. Resonating structures with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation are more stable. B. In electromeric effect, an unsaturated system shows +E effect with nucleophile and -E effect with electrophile. C. Inductive effect is responsible for high melting point, boiling point and dipole moment of polar compounds. D. The greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms, higher is the heat of hydrogenation. E. Stability of carbanion increases with the increase in s- character of the carbon carrying the negative charge.
sol: B ✗: the π electrons move TO an electrophile (+E) and AWAY from a nucleophile (−E) — reversed in the statement.
D ✗: more alkyl groups → more stable alkene → LOWER heat of hydrogenation. A, C, E are true.

pyq.q: What is the correct IUPAC name of the benzoic acid that has –OH ortho to –COOH, –Br next to the –OH (on the side away from –COOH), and –NO_{2} meta to –COOH on the other side?
sol: –COOH is the principal group → C-1. Number towards the nearer substituents: OH 2, Br 3, NO_{2} 5.
Prefixes go in alphabetical order: bromo, hydroxy, nitro → 3-bromo-2-hydroxy-5-nitrobenzoic acid.

pyq.q: The IUPAC name of the following compound is : HC≡C–CH_{2}–CH(OH)–CH_{2}–CH=CH_{2}
sol: –OH is the principal group (suffix -ol); it is C-4 from either end.
Tie → give the double bond the lower number: hept-1-en-6-yn-4-ol.

pyq.q: Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of given organic compound (X) ? X = CH_{3}–CH=C(CH_{3})–CH_{2}Br
sol: Main chain: 4 C with the C=C. Numbering from the CH_{2}Br end gives the double bond 2 (from the other end it would also be 2) and substituents {1, 2} vs {3, 4}.
1-Bromo-2-methylbut-2-ene.

pyq.q: IUPAC name of following hydrocarbon (X) is : CH_{3}–CH(CH_{3})–CH_{2}–CH_{2}–CH(CH_{3})–CH(CH_{3})–CH_{2}–CH_{3}
sol: Longest chain: 8 C (octane) with three methyls.
Locants from the left end: 2, 5, 6; from the right: 3, 4, 7 → first point of difference favours 2,5,6-trimethyloctane.

pyq.q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : IUPAC name of Compound A (a benzene ring with Cl at one carbon, NO_{2} ortho to it and NO_{2} para to it) is 4-chloro-1,3-dinitrobenzene. Statement II : IUPAC name of Compound B (a benzene ring with NH_{2}, CH_{3} ortho to it and C_{2}H_{5} para to it) is 4-ethyl-2-methylaniline. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sol: A: locant sets {1,2,4} either way; the tie goes to the substituent first in the alphabet (chloro) → 1-chloro-2,4-dinitrobenzene. I is incorrect.
B: aniline C-1 = NH_{2}; 2-methyl, 4-ethyl, alphabetical → 4-ethyl-2-methylaniline. II is correct.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

pyq.q: The IUPAC name of the following compound is : CH_{3}–CH(COOH)–CH_{2}–CH_{2}–CH(COOCH_{3})–CH_{3}
sol: –COOH outranks the ester → parent acid; the chain includes the COOH carbon (C-1) up to the CH bearing the ester: 6 carbons, hexanoic acid.
Methyls at C-2 and C-5; the ester is a methoxycarbonyl prefix at C-6.

pyq.q: Cyclohexene is ______ type of an organic compound.
sol: A carbocyclic ring without aromaticity (one C=C, not a benzene ring) → alicyclic.

pyq.q: IUPAC name of following compound (P) is : a cyclohexane ring carrying two CH_{3} on one carbon and an ethyl group on the carbon two places away.
sol: Lowest locant set: {1, 1, 3} (from the gem-dimethyl carbon) beats {1, 3, 3}.
Alphabetical order in the name: ethyl before methyl → 3-ethyl-1,1-dimethylcyclohexane.

pyq.q: IUPAC name of following compound is CH_{3}–CH(NH_{2})–CH_{2}–CN
sol: –CN is the principal group; its carbon is C-1 → 4-carbon nitrile (butanenitrile).
NH_{2} on C-3 → 3-aminobutanenitrile.

pyq.q: The IUPAC name of the following compound is : CH_{3}CH_{2}–CH(CH_{3})–CH_{2}CH_{2}–CH(Br)–COO–CH_{2}CH_{2}CH_{3}
sol: Acid part: C(=O) is C-1 of a 7-carbon chain (heptanoate) with Br at 2 and CH_{3} at 5.
Alkyl part: n-propyl → propyl 2-bromo-5-methylheptanoate.

pyq.q: Ionic reactions with organic compounds proceed through: (A) Homolytic bond cleavage (B) Heterolytic bond cleavage (C) Free radical formation (D) Primary free radical (E) Secondary free radical
sol: Ions come from heterolysis (the bond pair goes to one atom). Homolysis gives radicals.

pyq.q: Which among the following is incorrect statement ?
sol: When H^{+} attacks, the π electrons move towards the atom it bonds to: that is a +E effect.
The other three describe the electromeric effect correctly.
o: Electromeric effect dominates over inductive effect
The electromeric effect is, temporary effect
The organic compound shows electromeric effect in the presence of the reagent only
Hydrogen ion (H^{+}) shows negative electromeric effect

pyq.q: The shape of carbocation is :
sol: C^{+} has three σ bonds and an empty p orbital: sp^{2}, trigonal planar.

pyq.q: The correct order of the rate of the reaction for the following reaction with respect to nucleophiles is : CH_{3}Br + Nu^{−} → CH_{3}Nu + Br^{−}
sol: For the same attacking atom (O), nucleophilicity follows basicity: conjugate-acid pKa H_{2}O 15.7 > PhOH 10 > CH_{3}COOH 4.8 ≫ HClO_{4}.

pyq.q: The correct order of reactivity of CH_{3}Br in methanol with the following nucleophiles is F^{−}, I^{−}, C_{2}H_{5}O^{−} and C_{6}H_{5}O^{−}
sol: In protic methanol small anions are tightly solvated: I^{−} (large, soft, weakly solvated) is the best; F^{−} the worst.
Among O-nucleophiles, ethoxide (more basic) > phenoxide (charge delocalised). Order I^{−} > C_{2}H_{5}O^{−} > C_{6}H_{5}O^{−} > F^{−}.

pyq.q: The correct order of the rate of reaction of the following reactants with nucleophile by S_{N}1 mechanism is : (Given : Structures I and II are rigid) I: 1-bromobicyclo[2.2.2]octane II: 1-bromobicyclo[2.2.1]heptane (bridgehead Br) III: tert-butyl bromide IV: Ph_{3}C–Br
sol: A bridgehead cation cannot become planar: the smaller, more strained norbornyl (II) is worst, then bicyclooctyl (I).
t-Butyl cation is a normal 3° cation; trityl is resonance-stabilised → fastest. II < I < III < IV.

pyq.q: Match the LIST-I (Reaction) with LIST-II (Mechanism): A. Williamson Synthesis B. Friedel Craft Reaction C. Bromination of vinyl benzene D. Chlorination of toluene in light; I. Electrophilic addition II. Free radical substitution III. Nucleophilic substitution IV. Electrophilic substitution
sol: Williamson: RO^{−} displaces X (S_{N}2). Friedel–Crafts: aromatic electrophilic substitution.
Br_{2} + styrene: adds across C=C (electrophilic addition). Cl_{2}/light on toluene: side-chain free-radical substitution.
